defect_observations: C001 restricts the definition to families of integrable variables; Durrett's definition (p. 244) has no integrability hypothesis, but uniform integrability forces sup E|X_i| <= M+1, so no uniformly integrable family is excluded. Noted, not counted.

C012 does not give Theorem 4.6.10 its source name (dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations); C019 gives the alternative name 'reversed' only through an index entry. Names only; not counted.

C019/C020: Durrett's remark that the backward theory is particularly simple because the sigma-fields decrease is carried in substance (unconditional convergence statement; proof opens with Y_n = E(Y_0 | G_n)). Not counted.

C016: Durrett's statistical reading of Exercise 4.6.1 (sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean; law of theta = prior distribution; P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n) = posterior distribution after n observations) is carried in substance by the entry's 'normal (0,1) noise', 'additive sampling model', 'integrable prior variable' and 'posterior consistency' wording, with prior and posterior laws defined on the route (bayesian-updating-prediction lines 26-78). The explicit identification of P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n) as the posterior after n observations is not written in the entry; noted, not counted.
C015 is counted partial only for the source's evaluative remark; its mathematics (Exercises 4.6.2-4.6.3, including the endpoint extension f(1)) is complete.
